title: Dororo
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In Sengoku-era Japan, the lord Kagemitsu Daigo makes a pact with 48 demons for power, and his son is born without limbs, features or organs. Raised by a doctor who gives him prosthetics with a hidden blade, Hyakkimaru hunts the demons to reclaim his body, travelling with Dororo, an orphan thief whose bandit father stole from oppressive samurai to aid the poor. Osamu Tezuka's classic ends with enslaved villagers rising against Kagemitsu.
life_message: No one is born whole; a person becomes human by struggling against the wrongs done to them and standing with the oppressed.

content.note: Demon slaying, war, archers massacre enslaved rebels (Wikipedia; AniList War, Swordplay; MU Violence).
Disfigured infant set adrift, demons and yokai, a mother freezing to death (Wikipedia; MU Horror).
Dororo is revealed to be a girl raised as a boy; no sexual content documented (Wikipedia).
Classic with anime, film and game adaptations.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Hyakkimaru wins his body back by personal combat (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Wanderers outside feudal order; bandits and rebels (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: A father betrays his son; bonds of chosen companions instead (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Enslaved villagers overthrow the lord; Hibukuro robs samurai for the poor (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Demons, Buddhist prayer and spirit voices (Wikipedia; MU Buddhism, Shinto).

folkways.japan: Sengoku warlord society, Buddhist and Shinto spirit beliefs and the wandering ronin are drawn from Japanese history and folklore.

delivery.evidence: Publisher blurb calls it a thoughtful allegory of becoming what one is (Kodansha via AniList); message carried by the quest.

personified.ideology: Power and prosperity bought at any price
Take from oppressive samurai to aid the poor

delivery.note: The case against ambition is made through the son's suffering rather than speeches.

winners_losers: Hyakkimaru, Dororo and the enslaved villagers prevail; Kagemitsu and the corrupt samurai lose; sympathy goes to the outcast and the oppressed.
